narrative.overview:
This document covers the whole site: the homepage, the article reading page (/writing/<slug>), the writing archive (/writing), the bookshelf (/bookshelf), About (/about), and the shared foundation all five share. Every route is one editorial world; a personal site refuses the blog-template split where the homepage is designed and the archive, article, and shelf are left as framework defaults. Arrive anywhere and the same hand is recognisable: a light, tactile field of paper and ink where rigorous cobalt structure carries hierarchy while vivid orange appears as a rare narrative event.

The world is expressed twice, in two forms that share one material. The homepage is the Living Index: a horizontal editorial sequence of identity, two strictly separated indexes, and a panoramic artwork stage that answers browsing intent. Every other surface is a ruled sheet: a thin identity-and-navigation band over one near-black rule, then a Literata headline at page scale with a muted standfirst, then a ruled content field. The reading surface refines that into the Marginalia Sheet — one measured reading column with a wide outer margin carrying the editorial apparatus (the dated witness line, translations, and a contents list whose active entry takes the same orange star the homepage index uses), plus a section sign hung in the inner gutter beside each h2. Interaction enriches the apparatus but never carries essential identity, labels, navigation, or prose order.

Two seeds record the shipped directions, not content authorship: 526476f5 for the homepage, 61ce0048 for the Marginalia Sheet and the three index surfaces. Homepage prose, the professional descriptor, current-role details, contact destinations, project summaries, archive and bookshelf section copy, and generated stage imagery remain explicit placeholders until Mathieu writes, verifies, or selects them. Article prose, book data, and the About text are Mathieu's own and render unchanged. Final artworks must be Mathieu-authored or Mathieu-selected and keep the narrative role established by the temporary compositions.
keyCharacteristics: Cool uncoated-paper material with near-black ink, one paper-fiber texture, on every route.
Cobalt rules, labels, links, dates, and active structure; a deeper cobalt inside code.
Orange reserved for focus, the navigation underline, the single active mark, copy confirmation, and artwork events.
Sculptural literary serif paired with a compact humanist sans; no third voice and no faux-technical body face.
Flat square-cornered construction: rules, spacing, crop, and measure instead of cards, shadows, or chrome.
One shared header, footer, page-head masthead, and ruled ledger row across surfaces.
A true reading measure (52ch) with its apparatus in the margin, and a way onward at the end of every article.

rules.name: The Orange Event Rule
rules.body: Orange marks an event, never ordinary structure. One active mark per surface at most. Do not turn it into a broad background, routine text color, or second system of rules — and do not spend it on ordinary code literals.

rules.name: The Cobalt Structure Rule
rules.body: Cobalt tells the eye how the page is organized. Prefer a fine cobalt-derived rule or a cobalt label over filled blue containers.

rules.name: The Own-Colours Code Rule
rules.body: Code is set in the site's own palette on a transparent ground, so a block reads as part of the page rather than a pasted terminal. Never import an off-the-shelf highlighter theme or give code a dark surface of its own.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Literata carries identity and editorial hierarchy; Commissioner carries reading, navigation, metadata, and apparatus. Roboto Mono is for code and nothing else. Do not add a fourth voice.

rules.name: The Six-Rem Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type top out at 6rem, with tracking no tighter than -0.04em.

rules.name: The Descending Ramp Rule
rules.body: Below 1rem the sans-serif ramp is monotonic: the smaller the type, the smaller its job. Anything at 0.7rem or under is a label, a date, or a marker — never reading matter, and never a place to put a sentence a visitor must read.

rules.name: The True Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading prose is set at 52ch, not a nominal 65-75ch. ch is the advance of "0", which is 1.42x Commissioner's average character width here; 68ch renders 79-91 characters per line. Set measure by the real character count, not by the unit.

rules.name: The Segmented Index Rule
rules.body: Work and Writing always keep separate headings, lists, and destinations. Never interleave them into one stream, even when the layout stacks.

rules.name: The One-Panorama Rule
rules.body: The homepage opening sequence gets one content-width dominant image stage. Supporting Work imagery below may vary in size, but it must not compete with the stage in the first viewport. The four non-home surfaces carry no artwork at all.

rules.name: The Bounded Margin Rule
rules.body: The article margin is sticky and bounded to the viewport with its own scroll. Apparatus may never grow tall enough to push the reading column or to leave the screen.

rules.name: The Apparatus-Not-Navigation Rule
rules.body: The margin, the contents list, and the section signs are apparatus. The prose must be complete, ordered, and fully navigable with every one of them absent or scriptless; each heading link is a plain anchor first.

rules.name: The Flat Editorial Rule
rules.body: Separate content with spacing, rules, crop, measure, and tonal contrast. Do not introduce floating cards, ambient panel shadows, glass, or ornamental blur.

rules.name: The Square Field Rule
rules.body: Keep containers, media, code, and controls square-cornered. A rounded card or pill changes the visual language and does not belong in this system.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: A surface shows at most one orange active mark at a time — the homepage index star or the contents star, never several.

dos: Do give every new route the shared shell, header, footer, and page-head masthead so it is recognisable as the same hand from the first viewport.
Do preserve the cool paper, near-black ink, cobalt structure at its four thinned weights, and the rare orange-event relationship.
Do set reading prose at the true measure (52ch, 67-73 real characters) and keep its apparatus in the margin.
Do keep apparatus optional: the prose must read complete and ordered with no JavaScript, no contents list, and no section marks.
Do reuse the ruled ledger row for any new dated or listed collection rather than inventing a second row form.
Do set code in the site's own colours on a transparent ground.
Do keep placeholder prose, contact destinations, role details, section copy, and project claims visibly provisional until Mathieu supplies or approves them.
Do respect reduced motion and retain a meaningful, understandable still state.
donts: Don't let a route fall back to framework defaults or a second visual world; the quarantined legacy stylesheet belongs to the POC pages only and must never be re-imported into BaseHead.
Don't mix Work and Writing into an undifferentiated feed or uniform card grid.
Don't treat artwork as hidden navigation, decorative AI filler, or a separate gallery, and don't import the homepage's artwork onto a reading or index surface.
Don't let the article margin grow unbounded, become the only path through the article, or list translations as separate archive rows.
Don't introduce rounded cards, pills, gradients, glass, app chrome, decorative grids, drop shadows, glyph icon sets, or broad orange surfaces.
Don't spend orange on ordinary code literals, routine text, or a second system of rules.
Don't set reading matter below 0.7rem or add a type voice beyond Literata, Commissioner, and Roboto Mono.
Don't present placeholder copy, current-role details, contact destinations, or generated artwork as final.
Don't invent professional claims, availability language, a career timeline, or a funnel-style call to action.
